researchSnapshot.reason: Last 21-skill snapshot before the same-day expansion from 21 to 24 skills; pinned to preserve the issue's original research baseline.

classificationDefinitions.strong-overlap: PlotPickle already teaches the central craft territory with meaningful depth.
classificationDefinitions.partial: PlotPickle teaches material in the area but misses a material sub-area, medium-specific application or coherent treatment.
classificationDefinitions.gap: PlotPickle does not currently teach the area as a coherent craft subject.
classificationDefinitions.specialist: Useful optional or niche craft/case-study territory that should not displace the core journey.

highestValueGaps.reason: PlotPickle's current structure curriculum is feature-capable and structurally diverse, but it does not provide a coherent episode/season/pilot/series-engine layer.

highestValueGaps.family: Writers' room and collaborative television workflow
highestValueGaps.reason: PlotPickle has strong generic collaboration/versioning teaching but not showrunner roles, story breaking, television document chains or staff-room workflow.
No current canonical LEARN topic teaches sitcom/half-hour structure or comedy mechanics as a craft system.
PlotPickle teaches drafting, treatment and screenplay language, but adaptation choices and medium/format conventions are not a dedicated coherent lesson area.
The two Industry lessons establish roles, rights and verification habits, but pitching/querying, representation, options, credits, contracts concepts and career practice remain thin.

highestValueGaps.family: Scene craft as its own diagnostic unit
highestValueGaps.reason: PlotPickle distributes scene thinking across drafting, dialogue, visual storytelling and revision; a compact scene-craft extension could connect those systems without adding a new Path.
